correctness.rationale: Multiplying a degree-m trigonometric polynomial by e^{imx} turns unisolvence at the distinct nodes into ordinary Vandermonde unisolvence. For a positive single shift, the Dirichlet cardinal ratio subtracted from each unmoved weight divided by h is (−1)^{j+1}sin(δt)/sin((j−δ)t); for odd j its magnitude is below one since δt<(j−δ)t<π−δt. The moved weight is positive, and reflection covers negative shifts. For the symmetric pair, the equal positive moved weights are determined by the sum of their cardinal entries. Centering at the fixed neighbor gives an unmoved-k correction proportional to (−1)^k cos(kt)/(sin²v−sin²(kt)): off-center even indices increase their weights, and for odd |k|≥3 the positive correction ratio is less than one, by sin²(|k|t)>sin²t and cos(|k|t)<cos t. Thus only the central weight can vanish. Its normalized expression (1+cos t−sin²t/sin²v)/cos t decreases from 1 to −1−sec t through the specified zero. Strict convexity of arcsin(√2 sin(t/2)) gives monotonicity in K and the stated bounds via its slope at zero and its value at t=π/3. The absolute-weight mass follows by exactness on constants, and Taylor expansion gives the correct fixed-displacement orders. This is not a universal two-node threshold for arbitrary directions. The bundled floating-point moment-system checks were inspected, not executed; they do not prove the all-K signs.

evidence: The two-moved-node mirror covers odd N≥3 and every 0≤u<1 up to collision, including a quadratic noise blowup there; the single-moved-node mirror covers 0≤δ<1, including the unique zero at 1/2 and subsequent negative weight.

Yu–Townsend instead obtain central-weight negativity on sufficiently large grids by altering many nodes; Austin's thesis and Austin–Trefethen treat general perturbation, convergence and stability rather than these exact sparse signs in the passages read.

originality.rationale: Two distinct published Resultary statements substantively cover the two halves of the Finding. The inward two-moved-node theorem already gives the same complete signs, equivalent exact frontier, and amplification for a strictly wider parameter domain. The separate one-node theorem already gives the all-odd-grid positivity up to half a mesh and extends to larger displacements. The labels on the records do not establish priority; these are positive findings of mathematical coverage. Explicitly solving the existing cosecant level equation and differentiating the resulting elementary formula do not leave a distinct substantial theorem to validate or repair.
residual_risks: Comparing the statements establishes coverage, not the order of discovery or precedence; the directory dates alone are not used for that inference.
Literature comparisons are restricted to the passages inspected.
